etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English duracioun, from late Old French duracion, from Medieval Latin dūrātiō.

definitions.definition: An amount of time or a particular time interval.

quote.citation: 2022 November 16, Paul Bigland, “From rural branches to high-speed arteries”, in RAIL, number 970, page 55:
quote.text: To make matters worse, we pass through a torrential rainstorm, which makes window-gazing almost impossible, leaving me glad that the trip is less than 30 minutes duration.

definitions.definition: (in the singular, not followed by "of") The time taken for the current situation to end, especially the current war.

(finance) A measure of the sensitivity of the price of a financial asset to changes in interest rates, computed for a simple bond as a weighted average of the maturities of the interest and principal payments associated with it.
